title: AI checked all 13 million lines of Fermat's proof, a job that would take humans years - TCR 09/06/26
description:
Claude agents formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in 11 days, producing 13 million lines of machine-checkable code, OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra achieved its best observed score of 99.9% with the Provider Adapter at high reasoning on the ARC-AGI-3 reasoning benchmark where, at launch, every tested frontier model scored below 1%, and the Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft as Microsoft said 59,545 of 8.2 million selected Copilot conversations contained at least 16 words matching news content.

11:36 A federal bill to ban superintelligence
14:41 Close

This episode covers the Claude agents' 11-day formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem, GPT-6 Astra building its own symbolic world models to beat ARC-AGI-3, the widening copyright fight and Microsoft's discovery numbers, the MoChiAgent clinical system forecasting maternal and infant risk across 4.4 million visits, and the Sanders-Casar bill to ban superintelligent AI.

Four Claude agents finished formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem in eleven days, a job the field had expected to consume years, producing 13 million lines of Lean code, proving 29,500 intermediate theorems, with a separate comparator confirming that its theorem statement matches Mathlib's - the largest formal proof ever written. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra cracked ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark of unfamiliar games where, at launch, every tested frontier model scored below 1%, reaching a best observed score of 99.9% with the Provider Adapter at high reasoning and inventing its own symbolic rulebooks, while the best Provider Adapter result was 37.2 percentage points above the best standard-harness result, using a layer the results suggest well-resourced teams can reproduce in part and improve. The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft seeking deletion of the training data and the models, while Microsoft told the court that fewer than 1% of 8.2 million Copilot logs shared even 16 words with the plaintiffs' work. A clinical agent trained on 4.4 million visits forecast preterm-labour and placental risk from routine records and passed external validation on cohorts it had never seen. And a federal bill from Senator Sanders and Representative Casar would permanently ban superintelligent AI, a capability ceiling that would land heaviest on the open models that are the main counterweight to concentration.
